findings.reason: it would require the done-when to state the bound as a requirement and to carry §24's miss clause (attribute from a kept cumulative profile, file the repair as a new section), which is what keeps the plan's closing measure from closing on an unmet bound.
findings.text: §34 is the plan's closing measure ("§24 is the measure the plan closes on, but it could not buy its five passes per arm"), yet its done-when only requires the report to state each median against its 10 s bound, never to meet it, and it drops the miss clause §24 carried ("If head misses either bound, the node attributes the miss from a cumulative profile of the missing call … and reports the miss rather than passing"). The miss is plausible rather than hypothetical: §24's own report found the bare `obligation_snapshot.fleet_state` call — the exact call §34's first bound is read from — builds the ledger index twice at the after revision, a cost §23 left to "readers outside a derivation" and §33's write paths (`obligations.py`, `file_memo.py`) do not reach, so §33 may not bring the first bound under 10 s. As written, a §34 node that measures 30 s against a 10 s bound satisfies its done-when by writing the number down, and the plan closes with the obligation snapshot still outside `FRESHNESS_WINDOW_SECONDS` and no repair section filed.
